title: Federated Calibration Coordinator: artifact lifecycle, cleanup policies, and access matrix
creator: Priya Gupta
description: Build a 'Federated Calibration Coordinator' feature in Redwood Console that manages calibration runs (FP8/INT8), their produced artifacts (quant profiles, calibration traces, accuracy reports), and the lifecycle policies around retention, GC, and role-based access. This ticket scopes orchestration behaviors visible in Console: run creation UX, artifact immutability windows, promotion flows for validated artifacts, automated stale-run detection, and a permission matrix that lets platform teams delegate view/approve/publish actions without exposing raw model weights or secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: create calibration run wizard supporting single-run and campaign modes with selectable quant targets (FP8, INT8) and evaluation datasets
Orchestrator: runs are created with immutable artifacts for first 48 hours, then become eligible for GC per retention policy
Accuracy validation: automated post-run evaluation produces a standardized accuracy report (per-metric diffs, P0 regression flags) and blocks promotion if regression exceeds thresholds
Permissions: role-based checks enforce 'view', 'approve-for-promotion', and 'archive' scopes; actions are audited and visible in run timeline
Promotion flow: validated artifacts can be promoted to 'serving-candidates' namespace with checksum and provenance metadata; a manual approval step is supported for high-impact models
GC behavior: quarantine window and soft-delete (30 days) before permanent removal; admin can override via Console for emergency restores
API parity: REST endpoints exist to trigger runs, query status, fetch artifacts, and kick manual promotions (matching Console capabilities)
notes: We should avoid storing model weights in calibration artifacts — only quant profiles, KV-cache-friendly shard metadata, and evaluation traces are kept
Leverage existing signed-artifact pattern from PM-47654 for uploads; include manifest with SHA256 and producer job id
Cross-tenant artifact visibility must remain isolated; only metadata pointers may be shared in federated campaigns
Consider tagging artifacts with KMS key IDs when produced in Private deployments for stronger auditability

2025-02-18: Eng spike completed: prototype manifest format and immutable upload flow; found incompatibility with legacy artifact index — eng to add migration shim
2025-02-24: Security review requested for retention TTL and KMS tagging; security flagged manual approval audit requirement
2025-03-01: Console UI team implemented wizard skeleton; integration tests for promotion API started
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest validation and checksum verification
E2E: create campaign -> run calibration FP8 -> auto-evaluate -> block promotion on regression -> manual approve -> promote -> verify serving-candidate appears in model catalog
Chaos test: simulate object-store latency and partial failure during artifact upload and verify coordinator retries and idempotency
Permission test matrix across roles (reader, engineer, approver, admin) to exercise audit logs
data_retention_policy: Artifacts marked immutable for 48 hours. After 48 hours, artifacts are eligible for tiered retention: short-lived (30 days soft-delete), archive (90 days retained, access-restricted) or permanent (customer-managed export). Admins with 'archive' role can extend retention or request emergency restore. All deletions emit audit events and retention actions are visible in Console timeline.
permission_mapping: Reader: can list runs and view non-sensitive metadata and accuracy reports
Engineer: can start runs, download artifacts (excluding KMS-wrapped secrets), and request promotion
Approver: can approve promotions and mark artifacts as trusted for serving-candidate
Admin: can change retention policies, restore quarantined artifacts, and perform permanent deletes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): release behind feature flag to internal Redwood projects for live dogfooding
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for Dedicated and Private customers via console toggle; collect telemetry on run durations and GC churn
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all Hosted customers with migration script for legacy artifacts and default retention policy
Fallback: automatic downgrade to read-only artifact store for older runs if migration fails; alert run authors
open_questions: Should 'immutable window' vary by quant target (e.g., FP8 shorter than INT8) or remain uniform?
How granular should promotion provenance be stored to avoid leaking training data lineage while keeping reproducibility?
Do we allow cross-project promotion for internal platform teams, and what ACL model governs that?
What telemetry thresholds trigger automated quarantine (e.g., high regression rate across campaign) vs. human review?
